title: England Almost Lost to a Tiny Nation — Until Harry Kane Saved the Day
summary:
Can you imagine one of the world's best soccer teams almost losing to a country most people can't find on a map? That nearly happened to England! They were playing DR Congo, a team ranked much lower, and with only 15 minutes left, England was about to be knocked out of the World Cup. It would have been one of the biggest embarrassments in their history.

But then, superstar Harry Kane stepped up. He scored two late goals to give England a 2-1 win and a spot in the next round. Phew! The whole team and their coach, Thomas Tuchel, breathed a huge sigh of relief. If they had lost, it would have been as shocking as when England lost to Iceland years ago.

Now England faces a huge challenge: they play Mexico in Mexico City, at the famous Azteca Stadium. The crowd will be wild, and the pressure will be on. But England has some big problems to fix. They depend way too much on Kane and another star, Jude Bellingham. Other players need to step up. The defense is messy, especially the right-back position—four different players have tried it, and even a midfielder ended up there! Coach Tuchel keeps changing the lineup, and it's not clear he knows his best team.

Kane and Bellingham are amazing, but they can't do it all alone. If England wants to beat Mexico and go further, they need everyone to play their part. Otherwise, their World Cup dream could end in heartbreak.
why_it_matters: Even star players need their teammates to help, just like in a school project where everyone must do their part for success.

background_read: In soccer, sometimes smaller teams surprise big ones. In 2016, England lost to Iceland in the European Championship, a huge upset. DR Congo (a country in Central Africa) is ranked far below England, so almost losing to them would have been just as embarrassing. The Azteca Stadium in Mexico City is famous for its huge crowds and high altitude, which makes it a tough place to play.

WHAT: England nearly suffered a shocking loss to low-ranked DR Congo, but two late goals by Kane rescued a 2-1 victory.
WHERE: A World Cup match (implied in the U.S./Canada) and then the upcoming knockout game at Azteca Stadium in Mexico City.
WHY: The team is struggling because it relies too heavily on two stars; the defense is disorganized, and coach Tuchel keeps changing the lineup, raising doubts about their chances.
